g.text: Accuracy is more sensitive to meaning defects than grammar errors

text.style: font-size: 17px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526578

g.text: Drop from clean-passage MCQ accuracy · percentage points · all 7 tested configurations

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #172b3b

g.text: Both omission and mistranslation cause a larger accuracy drop than grammar in all 14 dataset × configuration comparisons.

text.style: font-size: 12.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526578

g.text: Positive = accuracy fell; negative = accuracy improved. Values are changes in percentage points, not percentage reductions.

text.style: font-size: 12.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526578

g.text: 30% is the nominal full-passage dose; local question exposure and severity are not matched across defect types.

text.style: font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526578

g.text: Word-by-word may affect meaning as well as fluency. This figure summarizes existing MCQ runs; it does not establish statistical significance.
